Hi Sam — quick technical answers + links, summarizing what we can include in the short SDK auth notes: 

Auth (short):
- Hosted: OAuth-based API keys scoped per project + per-route IAM; Redwood rotates short-lived tokens and supports customer-managed KMS for encrypting stored keys (KMS integrations: GCP KMS, AWS KMS).
- Private (VPC / on-prem): we support mTLS between control plane and private runtime; service accounts with JWTs issued by your IdP are supported; we recommend using your KMS/HSM to wrap private keys and configure 30-day rotation by default.

Routing + KV cache: 
- Session affinity: we allow sticky routing at request-level using a session token. Sticky routing maintains a KV cache for the session on the chosen runtime node.
- Cross-region cache: we don't replicate hot KV cache across regions automatically; recommended pattern is prefix-based caching + fallback to cold-start which accesses a shared embedding store (S3/Cloud Storage) to rebuild hot state.

Autoscaling + warm pool guidance: 
- For bursty weekly peaks, we recommend a 20-30% warm pool sized to expected burst TPS to avoid cold-start latency. Warm pool scales faster (pre-provisioned GPUs) and can be held during business hours.
- Concurrency: default per-GPU concurrency limit is 12 async sequences for the model family we demoed; with batching we estimate 40 tokens/sec per concurrency slot on A100-like hardware for typical short responses.

Embedding + rerank latency example:
- Embedding lookup: 8–12ms average per call (vector database excluded).
- Reranker model (small cross-encoder): 25–40ms P95 on the same pool if colocated; total added latency ~30–45ms P95. If you need <50ms total, colocate reranker and use quantized variant or smaller cross-encoder.

I attached a quick capacity calc and a draft mutual action plan (MAP). We'll also include a tiny SDK snippet for token exchange in the notes.

Cheers,

Adding a couple of infra-focused implementation notes from my side: 

1) Autoscaling windows: use predictive autoscaling for recurring patterns (cron-based warm pool on Mon-Fri 09:00–11:00 PT) and reactive autoscaling for unplanned spikes. Predictive warm pools should be tied to the scheduled job that generates spikes.

2) Concurrency & queueing: enforce a soft concurrency limit per customer (we set the limit at the ingress proxy) and use a token-bucket based queue for short requests. For longer-running generation (multi-step tool calls), use a dedicated queue with higher CPU priority and lower batching to keep latency stable for short paths.

3) Canary routing: implement percentage-based rollout with automatic rollback on latency/regression signals. We can open a temporary routing rule to send 10% to the quantized variant and 2% to the fallback cheaper region.

I'll be ready to share exact instance types and pool counts after Sam provides daily token counts.
